summary:
# NOTES: "THE BOYS OF GRAND PRÉ SCHOOL" (James De Mille; B.O.W.C. series; Lee & Shepard, Boston; Gutenberg #56232)

## Setting / cast
- Grand Pré Academy, Nova Scotia; Minas Basin; Blomidon (cliff, fog, "Cape"); Gaspereaux River/valley (enemy village; "Gaspereaugians"); Mud Creek; Horton Bluff; Cornwallis; North Mountain; Scott's Bay; Hall's Harbor; Pereau; Cape Split; Ile Haute; Parrsboro; Pratt's Cove; Five Islands.
- **B.O.W.C.** = secret society of five: **Bart** (leader, imaginative, improvises rhymes, jokester), **Bruce Rawdon** (strong, brave but superstitious about ghosts; leads Scott's Bay party), **Arthur** (Bruce's brother; Rawdons share rooms), **Phil**, **Tom**.
- **Solomon**, old black cook/servant, "Grand Panjandrum" of B.O.W.C.; dialect speech; afraid of ghosts; "Bee See Double"; "cool an airy 'partment" (kitchen); fled panic to room, barricaded.
- **Captain Corbet**: meek, venerable, dialect; former commander of schooner **Antelope**; has infant son ("babby"); wife **Mrs. Corbet** (domineering, away visiting); owns **mineral rod** (bought from **old Zeke**, "demon in human form"); copper coin "LOUIS XIV ROI DE FRANCE"; Hic jacet.
- **Dr. Porter**: headmaster, antiquarian, Museum curator; fond of boys; loves classics books (Euripides, Hebrew Lexicon, Longinus).
- **Mr. Long**: teacher, eloquent, defends Corbet at trial. **Mr. Simmons** (also spelled Simmops): teacher, mineralogy in Museum.
- **Pat**: Irish servant/boy, room in attic over Bart's room; mischievous; faked ghost noises; "Bedad".
- Others: **Jiggins** (superstitious, "solemn"), **Bogud**, **Billymack**, **Johnny Blue**, **Sammy Ram Ram**, **Muckle**, **David Digg**, **Harry Thompson** (small boy).
- Villagers: **Pieter Schwab** (Dutch justice of peace, "Rhadamanthus"); unnamed prosecutor (potato field owner); **Old Zeke** (drunk witness; "Old Zeke's rat").
- **Captain Pratt**: red-faced, jovial; saves Antelope.
- **Bennie Grigg** & **Mrs. Bennie**, Scott's Bay hosts. **Mr. Smalley**, **Mr. Atkins** (named, not met). **Mr. Slocum** (owner of owl). **ole scissa grinda** (donkey seller). Donkey = Dr. Porter's.
- Gaspereaugian "big fellow" (wrestler; Bart earlier hit his eye with snowball).
- Wade (mate; wife "Gipson").

## BOOK I
- Last day of spring recess at camp in woods. Dam water-tight, pool full. Solomon brings lunch (turkeys, mutton pies, hoe-cakes, ham, ginger-beer, doughnuts); refuses to stay ("De doctor'd knock my ole head off"); "Far well, mos wos'ful."
- Weapons debated (clubs, Chinese crackers, boomerangs, lassos, cannon); chosen: bows, arrows, willow whistles, made with jackknives (ash bow, spruce shaft).
- Corbet appears at camp (Bart: "Who goes there?" x3, "Speak or--I'll fire!"). Baby is "kickin an crowin." Corbet has been "nussin" baby.
- Mineral rod: "It's a diskivery… It's a mineral rod!" Found it last year; motive = baby; can't tell Mrs. Corbet. Hint of "Frenchmen's" money.
- Corbet pulls out ~50 junk items from hat (button, knife, string, tobacco, "Bonaparte's Oraculum," squirrel's tail, etc.); finds copper coin "LOUIS XIV. ROI DE FRANCE."
- Corbet: rod turned down hard at one French cellar; wants partners to dig.
- Bart: Acadians hoarded money (Benedict Bellefontaine, wealthiest farmer of Grand Pré).
- Target: "Old French Orchard" behind Academy.

## BOOK II
- Hill description: Grand Pré from above; Basin of Minas; Blomidon; changing scenery. Acadian history: French came first; dikes; British; neutrality; Acadians banished ("two thousand" from Grand Pré); Evangeline; poem excerpt ("Where is the thatch-roofed village…").
- Corbet in cellar; rod falls at center ("dozenth time").
- Debate: Phil "dig it"; Bruce wants morning; Bart insists midnight, twelve sharp, before cock-crow. B.O.W.C. alone; Captain + Solomon included.
- Bart's "magic": lights in multiples of 3 or 7; seven inside circle; silence after first stroke; "Book of Magic."
- Decided: midnight, last night of holidays.

## BOOK III
- Midnight. Lights: 5 lanterns + pails, baskets, tin kettles (21 needed). Tools: pickaxe, 4 spades, "the Bust" (palladium).
- Corbet: "I feel solemn"; rod falls again at center.
- Incantations: Phil (English history, Britain/Romans); Tom (Euclid hypotenuse); Arthur (Arnold Latin exercises; "Balbus odifcabat murum"); Bruce (grammar list, dignus/indignus); Bart (Caesar "Gallia est omnis divisa"). Corbet objects: "downwright heathenism"; asks hymn.
- Bart's hymn to tune "Rousseau's Dream" ("Why did we deprive the Frenchman… / Awful tasks in Greek and Latin, / Algebra, and Calculus! / …In the Frenchman's pot of gold!").
- Bruce digs with pickaxe; hits metal (ringing sound).
- Sudden roar (shriek/thunder/howl); half lights go out; two figures flee; panic. Solomon bolts to room, barricades door with furniture, sits in bedclothes till dawn. Corbet ("O, my babby!") runs too.
- Bart: retreat or return? Bruce: "I'll go back to that hole, if I die for it." All return.
- They refill hole. Corbet returns, admits he fled home then came back. Snaps mineral rod across knee: "Don't you ever go a diggin any more"; "dreams of gold… like dumb idols to the moles and tew the bats."

## BOOK IV
- Sunrise. Boys exhausted at breakfast.
- Mr. Long: stone wall (taken as ballast for Antelope) must be rebuilt; owner vowing vengeance; reward = holidays rest of week (Dr. Porter agreed). Bruce & Jiggins unload hold; Arthur, Billymack, Pat, Bart help Mr. Long rebuild wall. Wall better than before.
- Afternoon: Corbet found on stone wall; Antelope on side in Mud Creek mud, masts downward. Corbet: "No go… that there schooner's a gone sucker!" "finger of Providence"; will devote himself to babby.
- Corbet served writ (damages from wall removal). Mr. Long: "I'll take the responsibility"; trial "day after to-morrow." Corbet kisses Mr. Long's hand, praises him.

## BOOK V
- Night noises in attic (above Rawdons' rooms; Pat's chamber at far end; cupola; 15-ft abyss over hall; loose planks as bridge). Bruce & Arthur search; find nothing. Jiggins, Bogud, Billymack, Johnny Blue, Muckle, David Digg appear; Pat: "Ye'd betther not."
- Bart suspects Pat. Bart spends afternoon secretly in attic; keeps findings secret ("I will… wait till the proper time").

## BOOK VI
- Trial at small hall; judge Pieter Schwab (fat, bald, Dutch accent). Suit: "illegal… felonious… removal" of prosecutor's wall; claim $500.
- Old Zeke testifies on "a horse"; Mr. Long's cross: could be a cow, sheep, dog, rat ("Old Zeke's rat").
- Prosecutor: 1 acre potatoes, ~100 bushels, ~$50, ~$40 net. Mr. Long: "perjury."
- Boys testify Corbet absent. Corbet: "I knowed nothin more about that thar stone wall than the man in the mune."
- Mr. Long's peroration: Corbet "nursing with his own hands—his baby!"
- Dismissed; prosecutor pays costs. Corbet hero; procession home.

## BOOK VII
- Next night noises again; Bruce & Arthur search attic, fail; go to bed.
- Morning: walk to Gaspereaux (fishing). Bart stays, to meet them at camp at 4 pm with provisions.
- Breakfast argument on attic noise: Jiggins/Bogud/Pat = supernatural/Acadian ghost; Bruce/Bart = hoax.
- Gaspereaux valley description; Ridge Road; feud ("town and gown").
- Fishing: Phil 7 trout, Bruce 4, Arthur 3, Tom 5. Cooked on coals, no salt.
- Walk through Gaspereaux; no enemy seen at bridge.
- Return: Gaspereaugians occupy camp; Bruce furious.

## BOOK VIII
- Bart & Solomon ambushed (~20–30 boys) on path; Bart tied (hands); Solomon tied. Basket of food seized.
- Bart's jokes; big Gaspereaugian: "You're the chap that blacked my eye with a snowball."
- Bart slips hands free, waits to free Solomon.
- Bruce arrives: "What do you want here?" Big fellow challenges Bruce to wrestle. Bruce gets underhold, lifts him, throws him into pool. Gaspereaugians depart: "Exeunt omnes Gaspereaugienses!"
- Bart & Solomon escape with basket; Bart: "sixteen minutes after four."

## BOOK IX
- Camp described (fir branches; pool; "jaw of the big fish" over door).
- Distant roar; boys rush to Old French orchard, leave Solomon. Roar near Dr. Porter's pasture.
- Donkey found (bought from ole scissa grinda). Bart rides; donkey ignores him; then brays "Hee haw!" = mystery solved.
- Solomon laughs; "Mas'r Bart"; "Grand Panjandrum."
- Repast resumed (third time). Solomon's "cool an airy 'partment" speech.
- Plan: dig again by daylight; Bart's songs ("Whene'er I take my walks abroad"; "Over Minas's Bay came the French to Grand Pré"). Shovels struck metal again.

## BOOK X
- Solomon's speech on dignity of his office; donkey mention.
- Digging by daylight; iron plate; Bruce pries up "iron lid."

## BOOK XI
- Treasure is actually an old rusty ploughshare. Boys comically "give" it around; Phil bequeaths to Museum.
- Also found: colter; 4 bolts; ox chain (6 ft); iron pot; 3 nails; 2 bits of iron; 2 spikes; 13 copper coins (one reads "UN SOU"); a bone (Bart: "Benedict Bellefontaine"'s).
- Presented to Dr. Porter's study; items laid on books; doctor first furious, then laughs; family joins.
- Doctor admires relics; Mr. Simmons & Mr. Long join. Bart tells story.

## BOOK XII
- Dr. Porter proposes Saturday excursion to Blomidon to find French fort and an amethyst.
- Three double wagons, six horses. Start 4 am. Cornwallis valley. Breakfast at North Mountain (scenery).
- Doctor's history lecture: Columbus, Cabot, Cartier, Champlain; Port Royal 1606; Jamestown; Quebec; Utrecht 1713; ceded; oath/neutrality; Halifax 1749; Braddock; expulsion (~2000 from Grand Pré; Boston schooners; families split; read Evangeline).

## BOOK XIII
- Leave wagons; carry 2 spades, hammer, basket. Doctor leads into primeval forest (wood left side). Fog descends. "Barrens" (fireweed, blueberries). Doctor silent and lost.
- Boys realize doctor lost. Reach edge of giant cliff; surf booms below.

## BOOK XIV
- Doctor's map; confident of course. Bruce: people swerve right in woods.
- Split: Bruce's Scott's Bay party = Bart, Arthur, Tom, Phil, Pat; Doctor's Hall's Harbor party = Jiggins, Bogud, Sammy, Johnny Blue, Billymack.
- Pat's straight pole; Pat chases porcupine; Pat lost. Boys shout, search, give up. ~6 pm.

## BOOK XV
- Dusk; snake fence; road found. Pat reappears: "wild turkey… wild duck… goose with four legs" = porcupine. Bart: "ghost… in the garret."

## BOOK XVI
- ~8 pm: Bruce's party meets doctor's party on road. Both asked same question. Doctor swerved left; both groups had circled. Doctor: "The cliff was right, but you were wrong."
- Doctor goes on to find house; surf booms; fish smell; back door; Bennie Grigg (stocking feet, tar-marked pants): "This here place is Scott's Bay!"

## BOOK XVII
- Bennie & Mrs. Bennie. Huge meal list (broiled salmon, ham and eggs, mince pies, currant wine, johnny cakes, etc.).
- Sleeping: doctor alone; Jiggins & Bogud on settee; Sammy & Johnny on straw; rest in haymow.
- Scott's Bay description: ~500 people; Cape Split; Ile Haute.
- Sunday: doctor preaches at chapel; admits he was wrong; "Bruce had been right."
- Monday 4 am start; reach wagons 7 am; home 11 am. School delayed: "Hurrah, boys!"

## BOOK XVIII
- Pat scares small boys (Harry Thompson). Bart warns Pat ("sleep on sofa"). Pat: "It wouldn't let you."
- Last holiday night supper in Rawdons' rooms; Solomon's speech ("finished your high an mighty ventures…").
- Knock at door (Pat with stick); toll of cupola bell; Solomon collapses; flees to room.
- Boys climb to cupola; string under bell; Bruce traces string to Pat's room.

## BOOK XIX
- Bruce jerks string free; boys laugh; leave string in place as trap.
- First day of new term: homesickness described.
- Bart's plan: use donkey as ghost against Pat. Carpet on donkey's hooves; oats/turnips.
- Donkey dragged upstairs (noisy); Bogud's door; Jiggins sees donkey, slams door. Donkey left near Pat's room.
- Pat pulls string; donkey brays; Pat flees to Bart's room, locks himself in.

## BOOK XX
- Pat confesses (ghost pranks; owl). Bart explains donkey.
- Owl: Mr. Slocum's escaped screech owl; Pat took it home; Solomon scolds owl "Mas'r Owl, sah," gives meat.
- Mr. Long (study under Bart's room) summons boys; lectures on dangers to small boys.
- Pat confesses everything; boys confess donkey; Mr. Long relaxes.

## BOOK XXI
- Captain Corbet enters with baby (wrapped), wants Mr. Long to see baby; Mr. Long hurries off ("I'm in a great hurry").
- Corbet laments ("He felled, like an evil sperrit").
- Dr. Porter: relics labeled. Bart upset: bone is "cow" or "horse."
- Bruce's speech; Bart's poem "THE TRUE THEORY OF THE BONE" (Parley Yoo; leg shot; buried under apple tree).
- Procession to Museum; relics deposited.

## BOOK XXII
- Doctor lectures on Acadian banishment: Boston firm Apthorp & Hancock; bills for "neutralls" ($ per head); Pelitcodiac River incident; St. John River escape.
- Louisbourg: first siege (1745) by New England militia; Pepperell; Major Vaughn & 13 men in Royal Battery; "L'audace"; second siege; French crushed at Quebec.
- Boys visit Antelope at Mud Creek wharf; Captain Pratt arrives (potato freight to Boston). Pratt: "Whar's Corbet?… a gone sucker? Course she isn't."

## BOOK XXIII
- Pratt says Antelope salvageable; needs help. Boys to fetch Corbet secretly.
- Pratt's rig: tripods of spars, tackles, lines to tree. Boys + Pratt + two men pull: "Up she rises! / Hi ho, cheerly, men!"
- Antelope righted; mud cleaned; new hatches. Pratt: "a coat o' tar."
- Plan to get Corbet down by sending Pat with false "testimonial" message.

## BOOK XXIV
- Pat visits Corbet; baby left with Pat; Corbet goes to wharf; sees Antelope; weeps; thanks boys.
- Pat fails to quiet baby (rocking, singing, crashing furniture, bowl of food). Mrs. Corbet returns; Pat flees.
- Corbet leaves on Antelope with potatoes; crew: 1st mate, 2nd mate, steward, carpenter, cook, cabin boy, boatswain, boatswain's mate, crew. Wade mate (wife Gipson). Corbet: "Should Captain Corbet be forgot…"
- Antelope sails into fog bank; boys shout good-bye.
